group.title: Health and medicine
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A sign that a person has an illness.
examples: A cough is a common {symptom} of a cold.
wrong: A symptom is the medicine that a doctor gives you.

words.meaning: A doctor’s decision about what illness a person has.
examples: The doctor gave her a quick {diagnosis}.
wrong: A diagnosis is the bill that you pay after a visit.

words.meaning: A written order from a doctor for a medicine.
examples: You need a {prescription} to buy this medicine.
wrong: A prescription is a free bottle of water at the clinic.

words.meaning: The amount of a medicine that you take at one time.
examples: Do not take more than one {dose} a day.
wrong: A dose is a room where patients wait for the doctor.

words.meaning: An illness caused by germs entering the body.
examples: The cut became an {infection}.
wrong: An infection is a vitamin that keeps the body healthy.

words.meaning: A medicine that protects the body against a disease.
examples: The {vaccine} protects children from measles.
wrong: A vaccine is a treatment that causes a disease on purpose.

words.meaning: Lasting a long time or coming back again and again.
examples: She has {chronic} back pain.
wrong: A chronic illness goes away after one day.

words.meaning: Sudden and severe, but usually lasting a short time.
examples: He went to the hospital with {acute} stomach pain.
wrong: Acute pain is a very mild feeling that lasts for years.

words.meaning: The process of getting well again after an illness or injury.
examples: Her {recovery} took six weeks.
wrong: Recovery is the moment when an illness first begins.

words.meaning: A letter from a doctor sending you to see a specialist.
examples: My doctor gave me a {referral} to a heart specialist.
wrong: A referral is a medicine that you take with a glass of water.

words.meaning: Medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body.
examples: He needed {surgery} on his knee.
wrong: Surgery is a kind of medicine you can buy without a prescription.

words.meaning: Treatment to help a person recover from a physical or mental problem.
examples: She goes to {therapy} to help her stress.
wrong: Therapy is a machine that measures how tall a person is.

words.meaning: The food a body needs to stay healthy, and the study of it.
examples: Good {nutrition} helps children grow.
wrong: Nutrition is a sport that people play on a hard court.

words.meaning: Extreme tiredness.
examples: Long hours at work caused her {fatigue}.
wrong: Fatigue is the feeling you have when you are full of energy.

words.meaning: Redness, swelling and pain in a part of the body.
examples: Ice can reduce the {inflammation} in your ankle.
wrong: Inflammation is a feeling of being very cold.

words.meaning: The force of blood pushing against the walls of the blood vessels.
examples: The nurse checked my {blood pressure}.
wrong: Blood pressure is the amount of blood you give to a hospital.

words.meaning: The body’s natural defense against germs and disease.
examples: Sleep helps your {immune system} fight infections.
wrong: The immune system is the part of the body that digests food.

words.meaning: A medicine that kills bacteria and treats infections.
examples: The doctor gave me an {antibiotic} for the infection.
wrong: An antibiotic is a medicine that makes a cold start.

words.meaning: A harmful lack of water in the body.
examples: Hot weather can cause {dehydration}.
wrong: Dehydration happens when you drink too much water at once.

words.meaning: A routine medical examination to make sure you are healthy.
examples: I have a {checkup} with my doctor every year.
wrong: A checkup is an emergency visit after a serious accident.

words.meaning: A patient who visits a hospital for treatment but does not stay overnight.
examples: As an {outpatient}, she went home the same day.
wrong: An outpatient is a patient who sleeps at the hospital for a month.

words.meaning: A person’s emotional and psychological well-being.
examples: Regular exercise is good for your {mental health}.
wrong: Mental health is the strength of a person’s muscles.

words.meaning: Treatment and exercise that help you regain health or strength after an injury.
examples: {Rehabilitation} helped him walk again after the accident.
wrong: Rehabilitation is the first test to decide whether you are ill.

words.meaning: An unwanted effect of a medicine, in addition to its main effect.
examples: Sleepiness is a common {side effect} of this pill.
wrong: A side effect is the main reason that a doctor gives a medicine.

words.meaning: Able to pass from one person to another.
examples: The flu is highly {contagious}.
wrong: A contagious illness cannot spread to anyone else.

words.meaning: The state of being in good health, especially as a deliberate aim.
examples: The company runs a {wellness} program for its staff.
wrong: Wellness is a serious illness that needs surgery.

words.meaning: An injury to a joint caused by twisting it suddenly.
examples: She has a {sprain} in her ankle.
wrong: A sprain is a medicine used to treat a headache.

words.meaning: A sudden serious situation that needs immediate action.
examples: Call an ambulance in an {emergency}.
wrong: An emergency is a planned visit that you book a month ahead.
